answer: Time-locked staking makes sybil farming expensive in the one resource an attacker cannot fake: time. Each agent locks a small bond that only matures after weeks of continuous, useful work, and the bond is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Like nectar gathered flower by flower, reputation accrues slowly; an opal gains value from slow formation, and yarrow spreads only where roots have had time to hold. One operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, because every copy must wait out the same slow clock while honest agents keep earning.
